name: KIRIBATI

flag.title: Flag of Kiribati
flag.note: Frigatebird soars over a 17-rayed rising sun

lead: Kiribati (say "Kiribas") is 33 coral atolls so spread across the Pacific they touch all four hemispheres at once. Most land sits barely 2 m above sea level. South Tarawa saw one of WWII's bloodiest Pacific battles in 1943. Today I-Kiribati people fish, dance, and meet in open maneaba halls — always first to greet each new day.
geo: Kiribati's 33 atolls are flung across the Pacific like confetti — yet total land is only 811 km², less than Hong Kong. The vast majority sits no higher than 2 m above sea level, making storm waves a constant threat.

Kiritimati (Christmas Island) in the Line group holds nearly half the country's land and is one of Earth's largest atolls. Only Banaba, a raised coral island, climbs to 87 m — a mountain by Kiribati standards.
animals: The magnificent frigatebird rules Kiribati's skies — and its flag. With a wingspan up to 2.3 m, the male inflates a shiny red throat pouch to impress females and steals fish mid-air from other birds.

Under the palms lurks the coconut crab, the world's largest land invertebrate at up to 4 kg — it cracks coconuts with bare claws and lives 60 years. The rare bokikokiko reed-warbler sings only on Kiritimati, found nowhere else on Earth.
culture: Every village has a maneaba — an open-sided meeting house with a soaring pandanus-leaf roof on coconut-wood beams. Villagers gather to debate, feast, and watch te mwaie dance where every finger flutter tells a story.

Dance styles mimic the frigatebird's glide: arms sweep low, eyes flash sideways. Eight distinct styles range from slow seated buki to vigorous standing katei — keeping oral history alive without a single written word.
history: Micronesian ancestors settled the Gilbert Islands over 2,000 years ago. Britain made them a protectorate in 1892, then mined Banaba's phosphate for decades, displacing the entire Banaban population to Fiji to extract every last tonne.
In 1943, US Marines stormed Betio in Tarawa Atoll; 1,700 Americans died in 76 hours, one of the Pacific War's costliest assaults. Kiribati won independence from Britain on 12 July 1979.
wows: Kiribati is the only country lying in all four hemispheres — north, south, east, and west — simultaneously.
Its Line Islands are so far east that Kiritimati is first to ring in every new year on Earth.
Two Kiribati islands vanished underwater in 1999 — swallowed by rising seas.
The Phoenix Islands Protected Area (UNESCO World Heritage) is bigger than California.
More than half of Kiribati adults smoke — one of the highest rates on the planet.
Kiribati has zero army, zero navy, zero air force — Australia and NZ provide defence.
Kiritimati holds nearly half of Kiribati's land but fewer than 10,000 people live there.

myths.fact: The 'ti' in Gilbertese is always pronounced 's', so Kiribati = 'Kiribas' and Kiritimati = 'Kirisimas' (Christmas).

myths.myth: Sinking islands means Kiribati will disappear soon
myths.fact: The government has bought land in Fiji as a long-term option and is investing in sea walls and raised platforms — the response is serious and practical.
